title: Pyspark aggregations optimization
question:
I have a huge dataframe with 3B rows. I'm running the PySpark code below with the Spark config.

spark = SparkSession\
        .builder\
        .appName("App")\
        .config("spark.executor.memory","10g")\
        .config("spark.executor.cores","4")\   
        .config("spark.executor.instances","6")\
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled","true")\
        .config("spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled","false")\
        .enableHiveSupport()\
        .getOrCreate()

df = spark.read.parquet("/data")
df = df.filter(col("colA").isNotNull() & col("colB").isNotNull())
df = df.withColumn("colK_udf",udf_function("colK"))

df_1 = df.withColumn("newCol", when((col("colA.field") == 1) & (col("colB.field1") == 2), col("colA.field1")).otherwise("colB.field1")))\
          ...
df_1 = df1.select(...)

df_agg = df_1.groupby("colA","colB","colC","colD").agg(count(*).alias("numRecords"),
                                                     sort_array(collected_set("colE")).alias("colE"),
                                                     sum("colF").alias("colF"),
                                                     sum("colG").alias("colG"),
                                                     sum("colH").alias("colH"),
                                                     sum("colL").alias("colL"),
                                                     min("colI").alias("colI"),
                                                     max("colJ").alias("colJ"),
                                                     countDistinct("colE").alias("colE"),
                                              sort_array(collected_set("colP")).alias("colP"),
                                              sort_array(collected_set("colQ")).alias("colQ"),
                                                     max("colR").alias("colR"),
                                                     max("colS").alias("colS")
                                                    )
df_agg.count()

I tried the code on a smaller dataframe with only 100M rows, and it worked. However, when I ran it on a dataframe with 3B rows, I get the error below when executing the last df_agg.count().

ERROR org.apache.spark.scheduler.TaskSchedulerImpl - Lost executor 1 on 2.2.2.2:
...
The API gave the following message: Pod ephemeral local storage usage exceeds the total limit of containers 50Gi.

I have already increased the pod local usage from 30GB to 50GB, but I can't increase it indefinitely. I'll keep getting this message for other executors, and the number of failed tasks just keeps increasing.

When I looked at the Spark UI, under the Details for the Job, I'll see Input going up to 50GB, and Shuffle Write going up to 150GB. When I simply let the program run for hours, the Input went up to 350GB, and Shuffle Write going up to 480GB, before I killed it.

My data should be quite skewed too, with the top groups (after groupby) being much larger than the other groups.

I've tried to cache df_1 after select, but that didn't solve the problem.

What else can I try?
answer:
When you handle a large dataframe, the default number of partitions generated by groupBy (200) may be too low and generate partitions that are too big. Try computing df.select("colA","colB","colC","colD").distinct.count. If the number of distinct values is much larger than 200, you may try .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "20000") and see if the job works. 20000 might be too big so if the job passes, try to reduce it. Obviously, it's useless to set spark.sql.shuffle.partitions to a value much greater than the number of distinct grouping variables because equal values necessarily fall in the same partition anyway.

If that still does not work, it might indeed be a skew issue. To verify it, go in the spark UI and check if some tasks take much longer than others.

If that the case or if you don't have much distinct values, try salting your data as proposed in the comments.
